_comment: Rig recipes. One entry per kind of creature; the fitter in autorig_blender.py
reads these and places bones on the mesh it actually measured.
Every number is a FRACTION, never a length in metres, so one recipe fits a
12 cm toy and a 3 m mech:
*_z / spine.*      fraction of total height, measured up from the feet
*_out              fraction of total height, sideways from the centre line
face.eye_h etc.    fraction of the HEAD's own span (0 = neck, 1 = crown)
'measured' landmarks (leg split, arm tip, neck pinch) win over these numbers
whenever the analysis pass found them; the fractions are the fallback for a
mesh too fused to measure. bird_biped's spine numbers are lifted from the
hand-built penguin rig that already streams, so a penguin lands where a

humanoid.label: Person
humanoid.description: Human proportions — head roughly an eighth of the height, arms and legs about as long as yours.
humanoid.examples: people, anime characters, elves, humanoid robots

humanoid_creature.label: Creature (standing up)
humanoid_creature.description: Walks on two legs but isn't shaped like a person — big head, short thick limbs, a snout. The safest pick for most AI-generated characters.
humanoid_creature.examples: cartoon animals on two legs, chibi characters, mascots, orcs

bird_biped.label: Bird (penguin, chicken…)
bird_biped.description: Upright bird: stubby legs low down, wings or flippers hanging at the sides, a beak that hinges open.

quadruped.label: Four-legged animal
quadruped.description: Stands on all fours, spine running front to back. Front legs drive the avatar's arms, hind legs its legs — the head still follows yours.

bust.label: Head or bust
bust.description: A head, helmet or bust with no legs. Only head and neck get real bones; the arms and legs VRM demands are tucked away inside, unweighted.
bust.examples: floating heads, helmets, mascot heads, busts

blob.label: Blob / floater
blob.description: No obvious limbs — a slime, ghost, orb or drone. One bendy stack from base to top, plus stub arms if the shape has any.
